purpose: Pinned source manifest for newly identified SOTA or emerging structural brain/head segmentation candidates considered for the Kate n=1 and test-retest benchmark.
critical_interpretation_rule: A recent model or broad contrast claim is not evidence of anatomical validity on this subject. Every candidate must pass runtime feasibility, label ontology mapping, visual QC, registered pseudo-GT comparison, and test-retest stability before being promoted.

paper.title: SIAM: Head and Brain MRI Segmentation from Few High-Quality Templates via Synthetic Training
paper.claim_scope: Whole-head/head-and-brain tissue segmentation from synthetic training, intended to be robust to contrast, resolution, and pathology.

noted_models: model 1: older 39-region segmentation, trained on 3 subjects
model 2: paper-described version trained from 6 high-quality templates

native_port.name: siamize
native_port.role: Native C++/ONNX port of SIAM v0.3 with CPU/GPU backends and optional Docker image.

benchmark_role: contrast-robust tissue and whole-head segmentation comparator
potential head/extra-cerebral tissue QC branch for 2024 3DI vs FFE
uncertainty branch via SIAM folds, TPM maps, and external TTA after common-space resampling
limitations_for_this_project: Not a FreeSurfer DKT/ASEG replacement; label ontology must be mapped before pseudo-GT scoring.
Upstream Python SIAM notes substantial RAM/GPU needs; local laptop RAM is likely insufficient for first-pass full-head inference.
Claims are from a recent preprint and upstream repos, so local validation must be treated as exploratory until reproduced on Kate and test-retest data.
tools.next_action: Add a guarded siamize/SIAM smoke wrapper, first on one 2024 FFE candidate and only on hardware with enough RAM/GPU; then map labels into the TTA label-ensemble evaluator.
